statements.statement: A schematic shows the exact physical layout of components on a circuit board.
statements.explanation: A schematic shows how components are electrically connected, not where they physically sit. It is like a subway map -- it shows connections, not real geography.

statements.statement: Schematics use standardized symbols to represent circuit components.
statements.explanation: Every component has a standard symbol so that anyone can read a schematic regardless of who drew it.

statements.statement: A schematic is comparable to a subway map because both show connections rather than physical positions.
statements.explanation: Just like a subway map shows which stations connect without matching the real geography, a schematic shows electrical connections without matching the physical board layout.
